items.title: Standing Order: Standing Order on Servicemembers or Spouses of Servicemembers Seeking Admission to the Maine Bar
items.content_text:
STATE OF MAINE 
SUPREME JUDICIAL COURT 
STANDING ORDER ON SERVICEMEMBERS OR SPOUSES OF SERVICEMEMBERS 
SEEKING ADMISSION TO THE MAINE BAR 
 
Effective August 3, 2026 
Attorneys who are servicemembers or spouses of servicemembers 
assigned to Maine and who wish to be licensed in Maine while they or their 
spouses are stationed here may seek waiver of strict compliance with the 
duration of practice requirement of the rule g overning admission by motion 
without examination, Maine Bar Admission Rule 11A(a)(2).  The Maine 
Supreme Judicial Court, the Maine Board of Overseers of the Bar, and the Maine 
Board of Bar Examiners are committed to working with these applicants to 
accommodate their unique circumstances and to expedite the bar application 
process to the extent possible when they or their spouses’ service brings them 
to Maine. 
The Court will consider requests for waiver on a case -by-case basis, 
depending on the individual circumstances of the applicant.   Servicemembers 
and spouses of servicemembers are encouraged to contact the Maine Supreme 
Judicial Court Clerk’s Office at (207)822-4146 for more information about the 
waiver process. Servicemembers and spouses of servicemembers assigned to 
Maine who wish to take the Maine bar examination but have missed a deadline 
to apply for the exam, should also contact the Maine Board of Bar Examiners at 
(207)623-2464 or execdir@mainebarexaminers.org for assistance. 
Promulgation Date: 8/3/2026 FOR THE COURT: 
 
 
   /s/      
VALERIE STANFILL 
Chief Justice 
 
Andrew M. Mead 
Catherine R. Connors 
Rick E. Lawrence 
Wayne R. Douglas 
Julia M. Lipez 
Christopher C. Taub

Maine operates a statewide system of TRCs, including Adult Treatment & Recovery Courts, Family Recovery Courts, Co-Occurring Disorders Courts, and Veterans Treatment Courts. The Aroostook County Adult TRC will serve eligible participants in northern Maine.

items.title: Federal court order requires 4 Detroit-metro Leo’s Coney Island franchises, owner to pay $515K in back wages, damages to 143 workers
items.content_text: DETROIT – The U.S. Department of Labor has obtained a consent judgment requiring the owner of four Leo’s Coney Island franchises in Clarkston, Dearborn, Livonia, and Sterling Heights to pay more than $500,000 in owed overtime wages and damages to 143 employees. The consent judgment resolves the department’s case alleging that the four Leo’s Coney Island franchise locations and owner Kiriakos Vlahadamis paid workers straight-time rates for all hours worked when they were legally obligated to pay them time-and-one-half their regular rate of pay for all hours over 40 in a workweek as required by the Fair Labor Standards Act. Investigators with the department’s Wage and Hour Division alleged that the defendants maintained two sets of timecards for employees to separate regular hours worked up to 40 per week from any overtime hours worked each week.
